messages.author: eb1bc5d8c49bfec7
messages.subject: Non-euclidean distance for multi-sessions
parts:
Hello,

I'm having trouble getting nedist to work for my multi-session data. I used the same script for my single session data earlier and it appeared to work. I'm using the script found in the secr-noneuclidean pdf.

I have four sessions, which are all neighbouring ranges, each range was sampled a different year. There is a large, wide river running through the study area as well as another large river on the northern edge. We know that these rivers act as complete barriers to movement for our species (a large ungulate). The script I'm using is below:

noneuc_mask2km <- make.mask (traps(CH), buffer = 60000, type = 'trapbuffer', spacing = 2000,
                           poly = rivers, poly.habitat = F)
noneuc_mask500m <- make.mask (traps(CH), buffer = 60000, type = 'trapbuffer', spacing = 500,
                             poly = rivers, poly.habitat = F)

userd <- nedist(traps(CH), noneuc_mask2km, noneuc_mask500m)
Error in rep(1, nrow(mask)) : invalid 'times' argument

I'm using two masks as recommended by Efford, with the alternative mask (500m) to base the calculations as the study area is very large (a few hundred kilometres) with lots of recaptures. I've done checks on my data when I brought it in and all appears to be okay. The poly = rivers is the rivers that are non-habitat. 

Thanks for any help.

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Non-euclidean distance for multi-sessions
parts:
Hello Samantha
I'm sorry it's taken me a week to get around to looking at this - maybe you have solved the problem?

The immediate issue seems to be that your inputs to nedist() are multisession lists (of traps or mask objects) rather than plain matrices or dataframes. Try just one at a time.

Can I offer some more general comments? I doubt that modelling barriers to movement will make much difference, and it certainly doesn't seem to be the major problem. If the rivers are barriers then do you not have separate studies on the two banks?

As it stands, your dataset is massive. However (i) re-detection distances are highly skewed or zero-inflated (most less than 1 km, some up to 100 km), (ii) animals are highly clumped. You knew this. I don't claim to know how to handle it. Skewed redetection distances can often be handled with an exponential detection function, but maybe you also have a problem of non-independence due to over-frequent sampling. If the clumping is due to aggregation at habitat features (rather than social behaviour)  then maybe you can use a density (mask) covariate to sort it out.

The very large number of mask cells and 'detector' grid cells is sure to bog down model fitting - probably you can achieve the same result with wider spacing.

Cheers
Murray

messages.author: eb1bc5d8c49bfec7
messages.subject: Re: Non-euclidean distance for multi-sessions
parts:
Hi Murray,

Our surveys were in fact done on either side of the river, two sessions occur on either side. I was assuming that multi-session analyses were the way to go for the data I have, but I could be incorrect. The data comprises of four "populations", but we know there is movement between populations, currently the range boundaries defined by government don't comprise of the entire area where they have observed caribou (looking at their telemetry data, there are multiple animals who move outside the ranges), so I was looking at doing a multi-session analysis to model neighbouring populations together, as even though there is limited movement between, it does occur.

My other thought (and how I started) was to run each session separately, as they were all flown independently (we have total sight coverage of the ranges). However, when I apply a buffer to the range (suggested buffer is between 20-30 km), the buffer occurs on the other side of the river, and there are other samples from the other range that occur within this buffer - do I need to account for that? Or would it be best to clip my buffer to the river, and do either side of the river independently? I do think single session is likely the best choice, as you noticed the dataset is massive and I'm afraid any models i run will take way too long to make it feasible.

Right now I have my 'mask' spacing at 10 km, and my trap spacing at 2 km - do you think trap spacing could be farther apart? I didn't want to place the trap spacing too far apart as that would decrease the number of spatial recaptures - but we do have a lot already, so maybe it would still give good results at a wider spacing.

Thanks for your help, and your suggestions as well.
Sam

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Non-euclidean distance for multi-sessions
parts:
Not sure I can add much without getting too involved... I probably wouldn't trust an analysis of these data using standard spatially explicit capture--recapture models, for reasons given before.
Minor points:
(i) if a 'buffer' straddles an absolute barrier to movement (river) then yes the mask should be truncated
(ii) the number of "spatial recaptures" per se is not critical to estimate precision (of course, you do need _some_); in my experience it's the total number of recaptures that matters.
Murray
